tools.name: login_and_register_push_notifications
tools.description: Clannit auth login (email + password). Returns JWT in step_1_body_data_token. Requires step_1_body_email and step_1_body_password — collect via collect_user_input or emit_display input BEFORE calling this pipeline. Chat/Android sessions do not register push tokens.

tools.name: fetch_notifications
tools.description: Notifications feed for the logged-in resident, including past guest invites created (names, codes, times). Use for: notifications, invite history, guest-invite activity, check my history. Auth probe before create_guest_invite. GET /notification (steps 1, 2, 15).

tools.name: fetch_guest_invite_advertisements
tools.description: Marketing/promo advertisement cards for guest invites on the estate (image + open ad link). Do NOT use for invite history, sent invite links, or visitor list — use fetch_notifications instead. GET .../guest-invite/advert (steps 1, 16, 17). Agent-only; hidden from chat suggestion buttons.

tools.name: create_guest_invite
tools.description: Create a guest visit invite. Visit times are built in Lagos (WAT) by a CLI step — do not pass step_18_body_from_* hour fields. Collect guest first AND last name before preview. Always emit_display preview before Confirm. After success, display_data.invite_code MUST be the exact numeric data.code / g

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "login_and_register_push_notifications" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "login_and_register_push_notifications" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.detail: Description of "create_guest_invite" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp-bgpt-clannit" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch_notifications, list_forum_posts, fetch_guest_invite_advertisements · Private data: login_and_register_push_notifications, fetch_external_resource_file · Public sink: login_and_register_push_notifications · Destructive: list_forum_posts, fetch_forum_announcements, fetch_user_school, fetch_resource, fetch_user_profile_picture, fetch_forum_profile_photo, fetch_external_resource_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch_notifications, list_forum_posts, fetch_guest_invite_advertisements · Private data: login_and_register_push_notifications, fetch_external_resource_file · Public sink: login_and_register_push_notifications · Destructive: list_forum_posts, fetch_forum_announcements, fetch_user_school, fetch_resource, fetch_user_profile_picture, fetch_forum_profile_photo, fetch_external_resource_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
